```{python}
path_pseudobulk = PSEUDOBULK_FILE
path_manifest = MANIFEST
path_contrasts = str(CONTRASTS_FILE).strip()
sample_column = str(SAMPLE_COLUMN).strip()
group_columns = [column.strip() for column in str(GROUP_COLUMNS).split(',') if column.strip()]
padj_threshold = float(PADJ_THRESHOLD)
lfc_threshold = float(LFC_THRESHOLD)
n_label_genes = int(N_LABEL_GENES)
max_categories = int(MAX_CATEGORIES)
ntop = int(NTOP)

# The first entry of GROUP_COLUMNS is the group label column the pseudobulk was split by;
# every contrast is tested separately within each of its values.
group_column = group_columns[0] if group_columns else ''
group_label = group_column if group_column else 'group'

# padj is floored before the log so that padj == 0 does not produce an infinite y value.
MIN_PADJ = 1e-300

# Columns expected in a pydeseq2 results_df export.
RESULT_COLUMNS = ['feature', 'baseMean', 'log2FoldChange', 'lfcSE', 'stat', 'pvalue', 'padj']

# Columns of the contrasts file; the first four are required by assets/schema_contrasts.json.
CONTRAST_COLUMNS = [
    'id', 'variable', 'reference', 'target', 'blocking',
    'exclude_samples_col', 'exclude_samples_values',
]
REQUIRED_CONTRAST_COLUMNS = ['id', 'variable', 'reference', 'target']


def code(text) -> str:
    """Text as escaped inline code, for naming columns and files in prose."""
    return "<code>" + escape_html(str(text)) + "</code>"


group_label_html = code(group_column) if group_column else "the group label"
```

```{python}
# add table search function
# One handler serves every table in the document; the ids of the box and of the table it
# filters are passed in, which is what keeps a search local to its own table.

html = """
<script>
function searchTable(inputId, containerId) {
    let input = document.getElementById(inputId).value.toLowerCase();
    let rows = document.querySelectorAll('#' + containerId + ' tbody tr');
    rows.forEach(row => {
        let rowText = row.textContent.toLowerCase();

        if (rowText.includes(input)) {
            row.style.display = '';
        } else {
            row.style.display = 'none';
        }
    });
}

function sortTable(containerId, colIndex) {
    let table = document.querySelector('#' + containerId + ' table');
    let tbody = table.tBodies[0];
    let rows = Array.from(tbody.rows);

    // Clicking the column that is already sorted reverses it, any other column starts ascending.
    let sorted = table.getAttribute('data-sort-col');
    let ascending = !(sorted === String(colIndex) && table.getAttribute('data-sort-dir') === 'asc');

    let cell = row => row.cells[colIndex].textContent.trim();
    let numeric = rows.every(row => cell(row) === '' || !isNaN(parseFloat(cell(row))));

    rows.sort((a, b) => {
        let x = cell(a);
        let y = cell(b);
        let order = numeric ? parseFloat(x) - parseFloat(y) : x.localeCompare(y);
        return ascending ? order : -order;
    });

    rows.forEach(row => tbody.appendChild(row));
    table.setAttribute('data-sort-col', colIndex);
    table.setAttribute('data-sort-dir', ascending ? 'asc' : 'desc');
}
</script>
"""
display(HTML(html))
```

```{python}
# helper functions for creating HTML table

def sortable_headers(table_html: str, table_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Turn the header cells of a rendered table into sort handles.

    Every `<th>` of the header row gets an onclick calling `sortTable` with its own column
    index, so a reader can order the genes by fold change, p-value or any other column. The
    handler decides numeric or text ordering from the values themselves, which is why the
    column type does not have to be passed on here.
    """
    header = re.search(r'<thead>.*?</thead>', table_html, flags=re.DOTALL)
    if header is None:
        return table_html

    index = itertools.count()

    def handle(match):
        return (
            "<th style='cursor: pointer' title='Click to sort' onclick=\"sortTable('"
            + table_name + "', " + str(next(index)) + ")\">" + match.group(1) + " &#8645;</th>"
        )

    return table_html.replace(
        header.group(0), re.sub(r'<th>(.*?)</th>', handle, header.group(0), flags=re.DOTALL)
    )


def create_search_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame, search_text: str,
                             sbox_name: str, table_name: str, ntop: int=100,
                             lookupFunction: str="searchTable") -> str:
    """
    Creates HTML string for searchable table

    Parameters
    ----------
    df: pd.DataFrame
        Pandas DataFrame to be turned into searchable table
    search_text: str
        Text that will be displayed in search box before typing
    sbox_name: str
        Unique searchbox ID that will be assigned
    table_name: str
        Unique table ID that will be assigned
    ntop: int
        Limit the number of rows to this number to avoid giant HTMLs
    lookupFunction: str
        JavaScript function for text search, has to be defined beforehand.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        HTML table string that can be displayed with IPython.display.HTML
    """

    # input search box
    table_html = "<input type='text' id='" + sbox_name + "' onkeyup=\"" + lookupFunction + "('" + sbox_name + "', '" + table_name + "')\" "
    table_html += "placeholder='" + search_text + "'"
    table_html += "style='width: 100%; max-width: 300px; padding: 10px; margin-top: 12px; font-family: sans-serif; border: 1px solid #D1D5DB; border-radius: 4px;'>"

    # table, with every header cell wired to the sort handler of its own column
    table_body = sortable_headers(df.to_html(index=False, max_rows=ntop), table_name)
    table_html += "<div id=" + table_name + " style='overflow-y: scroll; max-height: 400px'>" + table_body + "</div>"

    return table_html


def inline_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
    """
    A small plain table on a single line, for printing from an `output: asis` cell.

    The rendered table is printed as a raw HTML block of the markdown. to_html indents its
    rows, and pandoc reads a run of 4+ spaces inside the block as an indented code block,
    which ends the raw HTML after the first header cell. Removing only the newlines is not
    enough, as the indentation then remains between the tags; every line is therefore
    stripped before the lines are joined.
    """
    return ''.join(line.strip() for line in df.to_html(index=False).splitlines())
```

```{python}
def split_list(value: str) -> list:
    """Comma-separated contrasts file entry as a list, empty entries dropped."""
    return [item.strip() for item in str(value).split(',') if item.strip()]


def read_contrasts(path: str):
    """
    Read the contrasts file of the run.

    Returns (dataframe, message). Exactly one of the two is None: a missing, empty or
    malformed file yields a message that is reported in place of the table. Optional
    columns absent from the file are added as empty strings, and the literal 'null' is read
    as empty, as the differential expression template does.
    """
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, f"The contrasts file {code(path)} is missing, so the contrasts cannot be listed."
    if os.path.getsize(path) == 0:
        return None, f"The contrasts file {code(path)} is empty, so the contrasts cannot be listed."

    try:
        contrasts = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", dtype=str, keep_default_na=False)
    except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError):
        return None, f"The contrasts file {code(path)} could not be parsed, so the contrasts cannot be listed."

    contrasts.columns = [str(column).strip() for column in contrasts.columns]
    missing = [column for column in REQUIRED_CONTRAST_COLUMNS if column not in contrasts.columns]
    if missing:
        return None, (
            f"The contrasts file {code(path)} is missing the column(s) "
            f"{', '.join(code(column) for column in missing)}, so the contrasts cannot be listed."
        )

    contrasts = contrasts.reindex(columns=CONTRAST_COLUMNS, fill_value='')
    for column in CONTRAST_COLUMNS:
        contrasts[column] = contrasts[column].astype(str).str.strip().replace('null', '')
    contrasts = contrasts[contrasts['id'] != '']

    if contrasts.empty:
        return None, f"The contrasts file {code(path)} contains no contrasts."

    return contrasts.reset_index(drop=True), None


def describe_exclusion(column: str, values: list) -> str:
    """The samples a contrast leaves out, in words."""
    if column and values:
        return f"{column} in {', '.join(values)}"
    if column or values:
        # The differential expression template only excludes when both are set.
        return "— (exclude_samples_col and exclude_samples_values must both be set; none excluded)"
    return "—"


def describe_contrasts(contrasts: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One readable row per contrast, with the direction of the fold change spelled out."""
    rows = []
    for _, contrast in contrasts.iterrows():
        blocking = split_list(contrast['blocking'])
        rows.append({
            'contrast': contrast['id'],
            'variable': contrast['variable'],
            'target': contrast['target'],
            'reference': contrast['reference'],
            'log2 fold change': (
                f"> 0: higher in {contrast['target']} than in {contrast['reference']}"
            ),
            'blocking': ', '.join(blocking) if blocking else '—',
            'excluded samples': describe_exclusion(
                contrast['exclude_samples_col'], split_list(contrast['exclude_samples_values'])
            ),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def read_manifest(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Read the headerless three column manifest: filename, group label instance, contrast.

    Grouping comes from the manifest rather than from the file names, because ids may
    themselves contain underscores and would be ambiguous to parse.
    """
    columns = ['filename', 'group', 'contrast']

    if not os.path.exists(path) or os.path.getsize(path) == 0:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)

    try:
        manifest = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t", header=None, names=columns, dtype=str)
    except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError):
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)

    manifest = manifest.dropna(subset=['filename'])
    manifest['group'] = manifest['group'].fillna('NA')
    manifest['contrast'] = manifest['contrast'].fillna('NA')

    return manifest


def read_results(path: str):
    """
    Read one pydeseq2 result table.

    Returns (dataframe, message). Exactly one of the two is None: a missing, empty or
    malformed file yields a message that is reported in place of the plot.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is missing."
    if os.path.getsize(path) == 0:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is empty."

    try:
        results = pd.read_csv(path, sep="\t")
    except (pd.errors.EmptyDataError, pd.errors.ParserError):
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> could not be parsed."

    if results.empty:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> contains no rows."

    missing = [column for column in RESULT_COLUMNS if column not in results.columns]
    if missing:
        return None, f"Result file <code>{path}</code> is missing the column(s): {', '.join(missing)}."

    return results, None


def tested_results(path: str):
    """
    Read one result table and keep the genes that can be placed on a volcano plot.

    pydeseq2 writes NaN padj for independently filtered genes; those cannot be placed on a
    -log10 axis and are dropped. Returns (dataframe, n_total, message), where n_total is
    the number of genes in the file. The dataframe is None, and the message says why, when
    there is nothing left to plot.
    """
    results, message = read_results(path)
    if results is None:
        return None, 0, message

    n_total = len(results)
    results = results.dropna(subset=['padj', 'log2FoldChange'])

    if results.empty:
        return None, n_total, (
            f"All {n_total} gene(s) in <code>{path}</code> have a missing adjusted p-value."
        )

    return results, n_total, None


def significant_genes(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """
    The significance rule of this report: padj below and |log2FoldChange| above threshold.

    The volcano plots, the gene tables and the up/down counts all use this one mask.
    """
    return (results['padj'] < padj_threshold) & (results['log2FoldChange'].abs() > lfc_threshold)


def count_significant(results: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple:
    """Number of significant up- and down-regulated genes."""
    significant = significant_genes(results)
    lfc = results['log2FoldChange']
    return int((significant & (lfc > 0)).sum()), int((significant & (lfc < 0)).sum())


def order_by_contrast(table: pd.DataFrame, contrast_ids: list) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Rows ordered by the position of their contrast in the contrasts file.

    Contrasts that are not in the file (or when there is no file) follow, alphabetically.
    """
    position = {contrast: index for index, contrast in enumerate(contrast_ids)}
    key = table['contrast'].map(position).fillna(len(position))
    return (
        table.assign(_order=key)
        .sort_values(['_order', 'contrast'], kind='stable')
        .drop(columns='_order')
    )


SKIPPED_NOTE = "skipped by the minimum sample guard (no result table)"
NO_RESULTS_NOTE = "no usable results (see the contrast below)"


def summarise_results(manifest: pd.DataFrame, contrast_ids: list) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    One row per group label instance and contrast, with significant up/down and tested genes.

    The group label instances are those of the manifest. A contrast of the contrasts file
    that has no result for an instance was skipped for it by the minimum sample guard of the
    differential expression step, and gets a row saying so. Counts are display strings,
    with "—" where there is nothing to count.
    """
    rows = []
    for group, group_rows in manifest.groupby('group', sort=True):
        produced = set(group_rows['contrast'])

        for _, row in group_rows.iterrows():
            results, _n_total, _message = tested_results(row['filename'])
            if results is None:
                rows.append({
                    'group': group, 'contrast': row['contrast'],
                    'significant up': '—', 'significant down': '—', 'tested genes': '—',
                    'note': NO_RESULTS_NOTE, 'overview': 'no results',
                })
                continue

            n_up, n_down = count_significant(results)
            rows.append({
                'group': group, 'contrast': row['contrast'],
                'significant up': str(n_up), 'significant down': str(n_down),
                'tested genes': str(len(results)),
                'note': '', 'overview': f"{n_up} up / {n_down} down",
            })

        for contrast in contrast_ids:
            if contrast not in produced:
                rows.append({
                    'group': group, 'contrast': contrast,
                    'significant up': '—', 'significant down': '—', 'tested genes': '—',
                    'note': SKIPPED_NOTE, 'overview': 'skipped',
                })

    columns = ['group', 'contrast', 'significant up', 'significant down', 'tested genes',
               'note', 'overview']
    if not rows:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=columns)

    summary = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=columns)
    return pd.concat(
        [order_by_contrast(table, contrast_ids) for _, table in summary.groupby('group', sort=True)]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
```

```{python}
contrasts, contrasts_message = read_contrasts(path_contrasts)
contrast_ids = [] if contrasts is None else list(dict.fromkeys(contrasts['id']))

manifest = read_manifest(path_manifest)
de_summary = summarise_results(manifest, contrast_ids)
```

```{python}
if de_summary.empty:
    display(HTML(
        "<p>No differential expression results were produced, so there is nothing to "
        "summarise here.</p>"
    ))
else:
    display(HTML(
        "<p>Number of significant up- and down-regulated genes per value of "
        + group_label_html + " (rows) and contrast (columns): <code>padj</code> &lt; "
        + str(padj_threshold) + " and |log2FoldChange| &gt; " + str(lfc_threshold)
        + ", the same rule the volcano plots use. <i>skipped</i> marks a contrast the "
        "minimum sample guard skipped for that group, <i>no results</i> one whose result "
        "table could not be used.</p>"
    ))

    # A contrast listed twice for one group in the manifest would make pivot raise; the
    # first entry is kept, as in the group section below.
    overview_columns = list(dict.fromkeys(de_summary['contrast']))
    overview = (
        de_summary.drop_duplicates(['group', 'contrast'])
        .pivot(index='group', columns='contrast', values='overview')
        .reindex(columns=overview_columns)
        .fillna('—')
        .reset_index()
        .rename(columns={'group': group_label})
    )
    overview.columns.name = None

    display(HTML(create_search_table_html(
        overview,
        "Search " + escape_html(group_label, quote=True) + "...",
        "sboxOverview",
        "tableOverview",
        max(len(overview), 1),
    )))
```

```{python}
def summarise_column(obs: pd.DataFrame, column: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Value counts for one .obs column, returned as a two column table."""
    return (
        obs.value_counts(column)
        .rename_axis(column)
        .reset_index(name='number of pseudobulk profiles')
    )


def requested_columns(sample_column: str, group_columns: list) -> list:
    """
    The .obs columns this analysis is defined by, in the order they are reported.

    That is the sample column, then the group label column, then the variable and the
    blocking variables of every contrast - the columns the pipeline aggregated the
    pseudobulk over. Nothing else in .obs is tabulated. The order is the order they were
    passed in, and a column named twice (a contrast variable that is also the group label,
    say) is kept only at its first position.
    """
    seen = set()
    columns = []
    for column in ([sample_column] if sample_column else []) + list(group_columns):
        if column and column not in seen:
            seen.add(column)
            columns.append(column)
    return columns
```

```{python}
obs = adata.obs.copy()

requested = requested_columns(sample_column, group_columns)
columns_to_show = [column for column in requested if column in obs.columns]
missing_columns = [column for column in requested if column not in obs.columns]

if not requested:
    display(HTML(
        "<p>No sample or group column was passed to the report, so no breakdown of the "
        "pseudobulk profiles is shown.</p>"
    ))

# The requested columns come from the pipeline parameters, so a column may be absent from a
# pseudobulk object that was built with different settings. That is reported rather than
# raised on, so the rest of the report is still produced.
if missing_columns:
    display(HTML(
        "<p>The following column(s) of this analysis are not present in <code>.obs</code> of "
        "the pseudobulk object and are therefore not broken down below: <code>"
        + ", ".join(missing_columns) + "</code>.</p>"
    ))

for column in columns_to_show:
    header = "<h3><font color='green'>Pseudobulk profiles per " + str(column) + "</font></h3>"
    n_levels = obs[column].astype(str).nunique(dropna=False)

    # A column such as the sample one can have thousands of levels; the table would be as
    # long as the object itself and tells the reader nothing, so only its size is reported.
    if n_levels > max_categories:
        display(HTML(
            header + "<p>Column <code>" + str(column) + "</code> has " + str(n_levels)
            + " distinct values, more than the " + str(max_categories)
            + " tabulated here, so no table is shown for it.</p>"
        ))
        continue

    table = summarise_column(obs, column)
    html = header
    html += '<font color="black"><details><summary>Click to expand table</summary>'
    html += '<div style="overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: scroll; max-height: 400px">'
    html += table.to_html(index=False) + '</div></details></font>'
    display(HTML(html))
```

```{python}
def volcano_png(results: pd.DataFrame, title: str) -> str:
    """Draw one volcano plot and return it as a base64 encoded PNG."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5))

    padj = results['padj'].clip(lower=MIN_PADJ)
    neg_log_padj = -np.log10(padj)
    lfc = results['log2FoldChange']

    significant = significant_genes(results)
    up = significant & (lfc > 0)
    down = significant & (lfc < 0)
    rest = ~significant

    ax.scatter(lfc[rest], neg_log_padj[rest], s=6, c='lightgrey', label='not significant')
    ax.scatter(lfc[down], neg_log_padj[down], s=6, c='tab:blue', label='down')
    ax.scatter(lfc[up], neg_log_padj[up], s=6, c='tab:red', label='up')

    ax.axhline(-np.log10(max(padj_threshold, MIN_PADJ)), color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax.axvline(lfc_threshold, color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')
    ax.axvline(-lfc_threshold, color='grey', lw=0.6, ls='--')

    labelled = results.loc[significant].assign(_y=neg_log_padj[significant])
    labelled = labelled.sort_values('_y', ascending=False).head(n_label_genes)
    for _, row in labelled.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(
            str(row['feature']),
            (row['log2FoldChange'], row['_y']),
            fontsize=7,
            xytext=(2, 2),
            textcoords='offset points',
        )

    ax.set_xlabel('log2 fold change')
    ax.set_ylabel('-log10 adjusted p-value')
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False, loc='best')
    fig.tight_layout()

    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buffer, format='png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)

    return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode('utf-8')
```

```{python}
def table_ids(index: int, group: str, contrast: str, direction: str) -> tuple:
    """
    Searchbox and table id for one direction of one group label instance and contrast.

    The ids are built from the same identifiers the volcano loop iterates over, plus the
    direction, with every character that is not allowed in an HTML id replaced. The
    running index is kept in the id as well, so two tables cannot end up sharing an id
    when different identifiers sanitise to the same string.
    """
    stem = re.sub(r'[^0-9A-Za-z]+', '_', f"{group}_{contrast}").strip('_')
    return f"sboxDiff{index}{direction}_{stem}", f"tableDiff{index}{direction}_{stem}"


def group_anchor(index: int, group: str) -> str:
    """
    Explicit id of a group section heading.

    The heading text holds the column name, which may contain characters such as ':', so
    the id is not left to pandoc's automatic identifiers. Only letters, digits, '_' and '-'
    are kept, and the running index keeps it unique.
    """
    stem = re.sub(r'[^0-9A-Za-z_]+', '-', str(group)).strip('-')
    return f"group-{index}-{stem}" if stem else f"group-{index}"


def group_counts_table(summary: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The up/down table at the start of one group section; the note only when needed."""
    table = summary[['contrast', 'significant up', 'significant down', 'tested genes', 'note']]
    if (table['note'] == '').all():
        table = table.drop(columns='note')
    return table


def top_genes_table(results: pd.DataFrame, ntop: int, direction: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    The most interesting up- or down-regulated genes of one contrast, ordered for reading.

    The direction ('up' or 'down') selects the sign of the log2 fold change, and the row
    limit applies to the selection, so each of the two tables shows its own top ntop
    genes. Genes passing the same thresholds the volcano plot uses are listed first, and
    within both blocks the ordering is by adjusted p-value, so the significant hits are at
    the top of the table without the near misses being dropped. p-values are formatted
    rather than rounded because they span many orders of magnitude.
    """
    table = results[RESULT_COLUMNS].copy()

    if direction == 'up':
        table = table[table['log2FoldChange'] > 0]
    else:
        table = table[table['log2FoldChange'] < 0]

    significant = significant_genes(table)

    table = (
        table.assign(_not_significant=(~significant).astype(int))
        .sort_values(['_not_significant', 'padj', 'pvalue'])
        .drop(columns='_not_significant')
        .head(ntop)
    )

    for column in ['baseMean', 'log2FoldChange', 'lfcSE', 'stat']:
        table[column] = table[column].round(3)
    for column in ['pvalue', 'padj']:
        table[column] = table[column].map('{:.3g}'.format)

    return table.rename(columns={'feature': 'gene'})
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

if manifest.empty:
    print(
        "No differential expression results were produced. Every group (value of "
        f"{group_label_html}) was either skipped by the minimum sample guard or yielded no "
        "result table, so there is nothing to plot here.\n"
    )
else:
    # Counter over all (group label instance x contrast) pairs. Together with the
    # direction it keeps the ids of the searchable tables unique across the document.
    table_index = 0

    for group_index, (group, rows) in enumerate(manifest.groupby('group', sort=True)):
        print(
            f"\n### <font color='green'>{escape_html(group_label)} = {escape_html(str(group))}"
            f"</font> {{#{group_anchor(group_index, group)}}}\n"
        )

        # Up/down counts first, so the outcome of every contrast of this group, skipped
        # ones included, is visible before the plots.
        group_summary = de_summary[de_summary['group'] == group]
        print(
            f"\n<p>Significant genes per contrast (<code>padj</code> &lt; {padj_threshold} "
            f"and |log2FoldChange| &gt; {lfc_threshold}):</p>\n"
        )
        print(f"\n{inline_table_html(group_counts_table(group_summary))}\n")

        for _, row in order_by_contrast(rows, contrast_ids).iterrows():
            contrast = row['contrast']
            print(f"\n**Contrast: {contrast}**\n")

            results, n_total, message = tested_results(row['filename'])
            if results is None:
                print(f"\n{message} No volcano plot is shown for this contrast.\n")
                continue

            n_dropped = n_total - len(results)
            n_up, n_down = count_significant(results)
            n_significant = n_up + n_down

            image_string = volcano_png(results, f"{group} - {contrast}")

            figure = (
                f'<figure><img alt="volcano plot {group} {contrast}" '
                f'src="data:image/png;base64,{image_string}" />'
                f'<figcaption>{n_significant} of {len(results)} tested gene(s) pass '
                f'padj &lt; {padj_threshold} and |log2FoldChange| &gt; {lfc_threshold} '
                f'({n_up} up, {n_down} down). '
                f'{n_dropped} gene(s) with a missing adjusted p-value were excluded.'
                f'</figcaption></figure>'
            )

            # A plot without a single significant gene says no more than its caption, so it
            # is collapsed; plots with hits stay open.
            if n_significant == 0:
                figure = (
                    "<details><summary><font color='green'>Volcano plot — no significant "
                    "genes (click to show)</font></summary>" + figure + "</details>"
                )

            print(f"\n{figure}\n")

            # Searchable tables of the very genes plotted above, directly below the plot,
            # split by the sign of the log2 fold change. One <details> per direction
            # rather than one holding both, so each table can be opened and searched on
            # its own; the direction is part of the ids, so the two never collide.
            for direction, label in [('up', 'Upregulated'), ('down', 'Downregulated')]:
                sbox_name, table_name = table_ids(table_index, group, contrast, direction)
                genes = top_genes_table(results, ntop, direction)

                if genes.empty:
                    print(f"\n<p>No {label.lower()} gene was tested in this contrast.</p>\n")
                    continue

                table_html = create_search_table_html(
                    genes,
                    "Search gene...",
                    sbox_name,
                    table_name,
                    ntop,
                )

                print(
                    f"\n<details><summary><font color='green'>{label} genes</font>"
                    f" - click to expand table</summary>{table_html}</details>\n"
                )

            table_index += 1
```

## <font color='green'>Software versions</font>

The first table lists the software of the pipeline modules that produced the results in
this report, as collected by Nextflow. The second one is read from the rendering
environment itself, so it describes the software that produced the report.

```{python}
def pipeline_versions(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Software versions collected by Nextflow from the modules of this stage.

    The file is the collated versions.yml of the pipeline: one mapping per process, each
    holding the tools that process reported. It is flattened into one row per tool so the
    table reads the same way as the one below.
    """
    import yaml

    with open(path) as handle:
        collected = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}

    rows = [
        (process, tool, str(version))
        for process, tools in collected.items()
        for tool, version in (tools or {}).items()
    ]

    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['process', 'software', 'version'])


modules = pipeline_versions(VERSIONS_FILE)

display(HTML('<font color="black">' + modules.to_html(index=False) + '</font>'))
```

```{python}
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess

import IPython


def library_version(module) -> str:
    """
    Version of an already imported library.

    The attribute is preferred over the installed distribution metadata because it is what
    the running code reports about itself; the metadata is only consulted as a fallback.
    """
    reported = getattr(module, '__version__', None)
    if reported:
        return str(reported)

    from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version as distribution_version

    try:
        return distribution_version(module.__name__)
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        return 'unknown'


def quarto_version():
    """
    Version of the quarto binary rendering this document, or None if it cannot be read.

    Quarto does not export its own version into the rendering environment, so the binary is
    asked directly. The row is dropped rather than guessed when no binary can be reached.
    """
    reported = os.environ.get('QUARTO_VERSION')
    if reported and reported.strip():
        return reported.strip()

    bin_path = os.environ.get('QUARTO_BIN_PATH')
    candidates = [os.path.join(bin_path, 'quarto')] if bin_path else []
    candidates.append(shutil.which('quarto'))

    for candidate in candidates:
        if not candidate or not os.path.exists(candidate):
            continue
        try:
            completed = subprocess.run(
                [candidate, '--version'],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=60,
                check=True,
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            continue
        if completed.stdout.strip():
            return completed.stdout.strip()

    return None
```
